Proud to be a part ofChildren First Academy Trust
Vision and Values
Vision and Values
Eldon Primary School
Aspiration, Determination, Success
At Eldon we know that our children will enter a world of work that is ever-changing and increasingly complex. Our aim is to ensure that, throughout their time at Eldon, children become resilient, independent thinkers, who have the knowledge, the skills and the confidence to pursue, and succeed in, whatever path they choose.
Parents, staff, governors and children all have an important part to play in ensuring that Eldon is a truly inclusive school, where equality of opportunity and respect for all is at the heart of what we do.

Proud to be a part ofChildren First Academy Trust
Context
Eldon Primary School serves a diverse and vibrant multicultural area, and this is reflected in every part of school life. Our community is shaped by a wide range of backgrounds, experiences and languages, and we see this as one of our greatest strengths. Many languages are spoken across the school, and we recognise that each child brings a valuable cultural identity and a unique perspective to our learning environment.
At Eldon Primary School, we celebrate diversity in all aspects of school life. This commitment is embedded in our curriculum, our relationships and our daily practice. We aim to ensure that every child feels recognised, respected and included, whatever their starting point or background. Inclusion is central to our ethos, and we work hard to create a school where all children can participate fully and succeed.
Children join us at different points of learning, and we respond flexibly to meet their individual needs. We understand that some pupils arrive with gaps in their previous experience, while others may need additional challenge or tailored support. We do this well through careful assessment, responsive teaching and a clear focus on early identification of need. Staff work collaboratively to adapt provision so that every child can access learning and make progress.
We also have an ARP, Alternative Resource Provision for ASD, which is inclusive within the school, supporting pupils to learn alongside their peers in a way that meets their individual needs. This provision reflects our belief that specialist support should sit within a fully inclusive school community. It is an important part of how we ensure that difference is understood, respected and valued.
Our school culture is driven by respect. This is evident in the way pupils, staff and families interact with one another, and in the expectations we hold for behaviour and relationships. Respect underpins our approach to inclusion, enabling children to learn how to value themselves and others.
Community links are also a key feature of Eldon Primary School. We place a strong focus on building positive relationships with families and local partners, recognising that children thrive when school and home work together. These links help us to strengthen belonging, deepen understanding and support the needs of our pupils within the wider community.

Geography
Geography
At Eldon Primary School we use the HEP Curriculum to teach Geography.
The curriculum is ambitiously broad in scope, meeting and exceeding the National Curriculum through substantial cultural, geographical and religious breadth and representation. The KS2 requirement to compare three regions is addressed through a carefully developed body of knowledge, rather than a tokenistic unit. Across four years, pupils encounter diverse global reference points, including California and the Amazon Basin, the Rhine, the Mediterranean and the Middle East, Wales and London, the Indus Valley and the coastal communities of the Indian Ocean. These studies are strengthened by related historical and religious dimensions.
Pupils develop a multifaceted understanding of empires, conquest, oppression and power structures, including their links with migration and the varied cultural experiences of those affected by migration, settlement and conquest. Revisiting these themes enables pupils to understand that Britain has been shaped by migrations over millennia, involving diverse ethnicities. They also learn that accounts of struggle against injustice may be silenced, making the development of well-formed questions essential.
The curriculum is meticulous in its rigour, reflecting up-to-date scholarship in history, geography, culture, religion and worldviews, alongside philosophy and social science. Work on Islamic Civilisations, the Byzantine Empire, the Maya and the ancient Mesopotamians is carefully worded, distinguishing established evidence from informed conjecture and imaginative reconstruction.
It is highly coherent, with intricate horizontal and vertical links across subjects. By Year 6, pupils can interpret poetry, music and art within the context of Christianity’s history in Britain and the wider world. They can also relate Beowulf, the epic of Gilgamesh and the Ramayana, recognising shared features of stories that reflect changing beliefs about justice, peaceful coexistence and problem-solving.
Sequencing is deliberate. Repeated study of rainforests, oceans and land use prepares pupils to compare sustainable resource use and climate-change impacts by Year 5. High-leverage activities ensure that pupils think deeply, retain substantive knowledge and secure vocabulary through repeated, meaningful encounters.

Proud to be a part ofChildren First Academy Trust
Children First Trust
Children First Trust
“Thrive and Achieve Together”
The Trust is committed to laying the foundations to be successful life-long learners and positive local, national and global citizens of the future through our values:
Resilience – Commitment – Integrity
Key Principles of the Trust
To provide outstanding education for the children within our schools and beyond
We believe that children deserve the best education, regardless of their background, their ability or their economic circumstances. We believe that, through working together, we can raise the quality of teaching and learning across schools, whilst keeping each school at the heart of its community.
To provide wide-ranging opportunities and experiences for children from Edmonton and beyond, to develop skills for life
We believe that all children should have the same high quality opportunities in life, both in education and in the wider enrichment that we can provide. We will actively seek out experiences for our children which will enable them to grow in skills, understanding of the world and personal ambition.
www.childrenfirsttrust.co.uk
Children First Trustees and Members
Our trustees and members are a dedicated and experienced group of educationalists, local business people and community representatives who are passionate about helping the Trust go from strength to strength.
